title: The pro‐inflammatory signature of lipopolysaccharide in spontaneous contracting embryoid bodies differentiated from mouse embryonic stem cells
authors: Jennifer Scharmacher; Maria Wartenberg; Heinrich Sauer

abstract: Embryoid bodies from mouse embryonic stem cells were treated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) to model inflammation. LPS induced a pro-inflammatory response, including cardiac cell activation and inflammasome signaling, suggesting embryoid bodies are a useful model for inflammation research.

title: T Cell Stimulation In Vivo by Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)
authors: David F. Tough; Siquan Sun; Jonathan Sprent
abstract: LPS injection in vivo stimulates CD4 and CD8 T cells, with proliferation limited to CD44hi CD8+ cells. This response is indirect, mediated by APCs and type I interferon, and may explain memory CD8+ cell proliferation.

authors: Yazhen Hu; Xiaolei Wei; Zhiwei Liao; Yu Gao; Xiaoling Liu; Jianguo Su; Gailing Yuan
abstract: This study analyzed the transcriptomes of resting and LPS-activated grass carp macrophages. Four novel cell surface markers and two chemokines were identified as potential macrophage markers, with others indicating activation.

authors: Keita Yamauchi; Yoshitoshi Kasuya; Fuminobu Kuroda; Kensuke Tanaka; Junichi Tsuyusaki; Shunsuke Ishi...

abstract: CD69-deficient mice were studied for their response to bleomycin-induced lung injury. These mice showed significantly reduced lung inflammation and fibrosis compared to wild-type mice.

abstract: Corydalis decumbens (CD) was studied for its effects on LPS-stimulated macrophages. CD inhibits macrophage migration and phagocytosis, promotes M2 polarization, and inactivates the RhoA signaling pathway, thereby alleviating inflammatory responses.

abstract: CD69 expression on human monocytes was studied, and its cross-linking was found to trigger calcium influx, lipid mediator release, and nitric oxide production. This CD69 activation enhances monocyte cytotoxicity.

abstract: This study investigated the effects of lipopolysaccharides from *Porphyromonas gingivalis* and *Porphyromonas endodontalis* on macrophage polarization. *P. gingivalis* LPS induced an M1 macrophage profile, while *P. endodontalis* LPS did not.

authors: Sobia Raza, Mark W. Barnett, Zohar Barnett-Itzhaki, Ido Amit, David A. Hume, Tom C. Freeman
abstract: Transcriptomic data was analyzed to understand macrophage activation by inflammatory mediators. The LPS response can be divided into more co-regulated gene subsets than previously thought.

abstract: Peritoneal macrophages from BALB/c and C57BL/6 mice were stimulated with LPS to compare their responses. Different mouse strains exhibit distinct cytokine profiles and functional activities when exposed to LPS.
